name: Learning-Space Minor Closure and Euclidean Coefficient Spaces
statement: For a nonempty union-closed class $C$, the following are equivalent: $\varepsilon_0(C)=0$; every source has empty retained positive separator system; $C$ is an upper ideal in a learning space on the same coordinates; $C$ is a one-marker conditioning of a learning space; and $C$ is a nonempty pc-minor of a learning space in the inherited orientation. There is a unique largest ambient learning space. Up to signed coordinates and constants, $\eta_0=0$ characterizes exactly the convex-geometry ideals, and every one has coefficient space $\mathbb R^{d_C}$.
proof: Deleting all-negative clauses leaves an implication family whose empty-root accessible component is the unique largest learning space. Empty retained systems put every source in that component and make the original class an upper ideal. Conversely, upper-ideal closure excludes every positive missing pattern and empties the retained systems. Adding one marker realizes the ideal as a conditioning. Minor monotonicity gives the reverse implication, complementation gives convex-geometry ideals, and the one-sided scaling theorem gives the Euclidean coefficient space.
